changes.title: fix: two release blockers found by dogfooding v0.1.0
changes.description:
Found by running `chartula preview --tag v0.1.0` against this repository. Neither bug is reachable from the existing tests: the first needs a live API call, the second needs real pull request bodies.

## Truncation (`ChatModel`)

Calls went out without `ChatOptions`, so `MaxOutputTokens` was never set. The provider requires `max_tokens` and substitutes its own default of 1024 when absent. All three audience texts were cut off mid-word — the run metrics showed `3 calls, 3,072 out`, exactly 3 × 1024.

It failed silently. The run reported success, and the thorough check spent 56,712 tokens flagging the severed sentence as an unsupported claim — a real bug symptom read as a hallucination.

The ceiling is now always sent, configurable via `llm.maxOutputTokens`, defaulting to 16000.

## False breaking changes (`ConventionalCommitCategorizer`)

`MentionsBreakingChange` searched the whole body for `BREAKING CHANGE` as a case-insensitive substring, so prose *discussing* breaking changes *declared* one. Six of the thirty-three changes in v0.1.0 were mislabelled; none were breaking. #65 described a setting called breaking-change prominence and was marked breaking for saying so — the feature that renders breaking changes prominently became one.

Now matches the Conventional Commits footer: uppercase, start of line, colon-terminated.

## Verification

Both fixes confirmed against a real run, not just tests:

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rephrasing output | 3,072 tokens (3 × 1024) | 11,271 tokens |
| Text endings | mid-word | complete sentences |
| Breaking changes reported | 6 | 0 |
| Thorough check claims | 1 (the truncation artifact) | 0 |

265 tests pass, 9 new. The categorizer regression test uses the sentence from #65 verbatim as a fixture.

## Known, not fixed here

`RuleBasedFaithfulnessChecker` matches `\bbreaking\b` across the whole output and flags a breaking-change claim whenever the word appears — the same phrase-versus-assertion mistake, now visible because no fact is breaking anymore. The flags are advisory and do not fail a run, and separating a claim from prose that uses the word needs more than a regex. Filed separately rather than rushed in.

changes.title: docs: bring the docs up to what Chartula actually is
changes.description:
Phase 1 is complete, but the docs still described a project that was being planned.

## What was wrong

- **`Usage` was not runnable.** It called the commands "planned entry points" and showed `chartula preview` without the `--tag` and `--repo` they require.
- **The `docs/` folder was invisible.** All four documents existed and were linked from nowhere.
- **`chartula.example.yaml` showed 4 of 8 supported sections** - `github`, `labels`, `categories` and `review` were missing.
- **The status badge said "early development"** with 27 of 27 phase 1 issues closed.
- **CONTRIBUTING asked for "the .NET SDK"** - an older one cannot build `net10.0` - and documented four commit scopes (`collect`, `curate`, `render`, `check`) that were never used once, while the sixteen actually in use went unmentioned.

## What changed

**The wordmark leads the README**, switched via `<picture>` + `prefers-color-scheme` so it reads on either theme.

**Long-celled tables became prose.** Two columns of paragraph text collapse on a phone, which is where a README often gets read. `Why Chartula`, `Core ideas` and `Roadmap` are now prose and headings. The tables that remain (env vars, doc index) hold short facts and survive a narrow column.

**Added [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md).** The layering and the reasoning behind the dependency choices lived only in the code and in review comments, so nothing stopped a contributor from reaching for LibGit2Sharp or Octokit and quietly costing the native-AOT goal. It states the inward-pointing rule, why facts are established before an LLM sees them, and where each concern lives.

**Everything else now points somewhere**: a documentation index in the README, architecture and fixtures linked from CONTRIBUTING.

## Verification

- All 24 relative links in `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/*.md` resolve to existing files.
- Both SVGs are valid XML with no external references and no `<script>`; rendered to PNG and checked against a dark and a light background.
- Uncommented every section of `chartula.example.yaml` into a real `chartula.yaml` and ran the CLI against it: all eight sections bind, no configuration error.
- Every documented default checked against the value in the code.
- `dotnet build`: 0 warnings. `dotnet test`: 256 passing.

Note: the brand asset delivery note that came with the SVGs is deliberately not in this PR. It is in German, describes files that are not in the repo (`mark/`, `favicon/`), and states Chartula is "tiny charts for your terminal", which it is not.

changes.title: feat: report what a run does and what it costs
changes.description:
Makes the tool measurable, so the defaults can be decided by data instead of guesswork.

Every `preview` and `generate` run now ends with:

```text
Run metrics
  Rule-based check: 3 runs, 1 with findings, 1 claim, no tokens
  Thorough check:   3 runs, 2 with findings, 2 claims, 6,230 in / 130 out
    caught 1 claim the rule-based check missed, for 6,360 tokens in 3 calls
  Rephrasing:       3 calls, 5,437 in / 859 out
  Total:            12,656 tokens
```

## Does the thorough check earn its cost?

The indented line is the point of the whole summary. It pairs the claims **only** the thorough check caught with the tokens it spent catching them. Claims both checks find are excluded, because on those the thorough check adds nothing over the free one. Read across a few real releases, that line answers the question directly: consistently zero claims caught means the tokens buy nothing.

## What changed

- `Chartula.Core/Observability/`: `IRunMetrics` with the `RunMetrics` sink, `NullRunMetrics`, `RunReport` and `RunReportFormatter`.
- `ChatModel` reports token usage, because it is the only place that sees it. Usage is attributed per `LlmOperation`, so the check's cost is readable on its own; a provider that reports no usage still has its call counted.
- `ReleasePipeline` records both checks' findings in one call, because it is the only place that can compare them, and returns the report on `ReleaseOutcome`.
- Measurement is a side channel: the sink is optional everywhere, and a run without one produces byte-identical output.
- `docs/run-metrics.md` explains how to read the summary and make the keep-or-drop call.

## Verification

- `dotnet build Chartula.slnx -c Debug`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `dotnet test Chartula.slnx`: 215 passing (Core 177, Infrastructure 26, Cli 12), 21 of them new, covering check-fire counts, per-operation token usage, thorough-only attribution, snapshot isolation, and concurrent recording.
- CLI end-to-end: the real DI graph resolves the sink into both optional constructors, and the rendered summary was reviewed against the real formatter output.

Closes #26

changes.title: feat: add configuration sections for categories
changes.description:
Rounds out the configuration surface: category presentation is now configurable alongside the existing `labels`, `factBase` and `faithfulness` sections.

## What changed

- `CategorySettings` in the domain holds the category order, display names and breaking-change prominence, with `From(...)` parsing the raw configuration values and rejecting unknown category names with a clear message.
- `GroundedFactsFactory` is extracted out of `ReleaseChangelogGenerator`, so audience filtering, category ordering and display naming have a single home.
- `categories` section in `chartula.yaml`: `order`, `names`, `breakingProminent` (default `true`). Every section stays independently editable; untouched sections keep their defaults.
- `docs/configuration.md` documents the new section.

## Verification

- `dotnet build Chartula.slnx -c Debug`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `dotnet test Chartula.slnx`: 194 passing (Core 158, Infrastructure 26, Cli 10), 17 of them new.
- CLI end-to-end: an invalid category in the configuration exits 1 with `Configuration error: Unknown category 'nonsense' in categories order. Valid categories: ...`; a valid `categories` section binds and reaches the pipeline.

Closes #25

changes.title: feat(config): read chartula.yaml with sensible defaults
changes.description:
Closes #24

## What

Lets `chartula.yaml` refine behavior while the tool still works with no configuration at all.

- **`Chartula.Cli`**: `AddChartulaYaml` loads `chartula.yaml` (or `.yml`) via YamlDotNet and flattens it into `Chartula:*` configuration keys, layered **before** environment variables (env overrides YAML). All the section options (`llm`, `github`, `labels`, `filter`, `factBase`, `faithfulness`, `review`) already existed - this just adds the file as a source. With neither a file nor env vars, every option binds to its default.
- **`chartula.example.yaml`** (repo root): minimal, everything commented out - copy to `chartula.yaml` and uncomment what you need.
- **`docs/configuration.md`**: the full option set with defaults.
- Configuration errors (e.g. an invalid value in `chartula.yaml`) are now reported as a clear `Configuration error: ...` message instead of an unhandled exception.
- **`Chartula.Cli.Tests`** (new project, `InternalsVisibleTo` from the CLI): the home for CLI-level tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] With no `chartula.yaml`, the tool runs with sensible defaults.
- [x] A present config refines behavior; it is never required.
- [x] The shipped example file is minimal; full options live in docs.
- [x] Tests: cover the no-config defaults path and a config-refines-behavior path.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 147, Infrastructure 26, **Cli 5**): YAML flattening to prefixed keys, no-config -> defaults, a present config refining `factBase.depth`/`faithfulness.thorough`, absent file is a no-op, and reading `chartula.yaml` from a directory. Verified end-to-end: an invalid `depth` in `chartula.yaml` prints a clear `Configuration error: ...` (proving the file is read), and an environment variable overrides the YAML value.

## Notes

`chartula.example.yaml` is shipped (not a live `chartula.yaml`) so it is not picked up when running Chartula in its own repo.

changes.title: feat(cli): generate and preview commands wired to the pipeline
changes.description:
Closes #23

## What

Gives the CLI a real command surface and ties the whole pipeline together.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `ReleasePipeline` orchestrates the flow over ports only - read commit range (#3) and PRs (#4) -> build fact base (#10) -> render all audiences (#15) -> rule-based (#17) + thorough (#18) faithfulness + review (#19) -> write outputs. The **only** difference between the two modes is the final write step.
  - `generate`: writes `changelog.json` (all audience texts, #22), `CHANGELOG.md` (#20), and the GitHub release notes (#21) from the technical rendering.
  - `preview`: runs the identical flow (including generation, so you see the real result) but writes and publishes **nothing**.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: `chartula preview` / `chartula generate`, each taking `--tag` and `--repo <owner/name>`; a usage screen; clear errors for unknown commands / missing options; a readable per-audience summary. Pipeline errors are caught and reported, not crashed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `generate` produces and writes outputs.
- [x] `preview` shows what would be produced without writing/publishing.
- [x] Both give clear, helpful output.
- [x] Tests: assert preview writes and publishes nothing while generate writes outputs.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 147, Infrastructure 26): preview leaves all three writer spies **uncalled** and its `WrittenOutputs` empty while still producing all three renderings; generate calls every writer and lists the outputs. CLI verified end-to-end: usage on no args, exit-1 with a clear message for missing `--tag` / invalid `--repo` / unknown command, and `preview` reaching the pipeline and failing gracefully (`Error: Tag '...' does not resolve...`) rather than crashing.

## Notes

`--repo` is explicit for now; auto-detecting it from the git remote is a future nicety. The interactive console reviewer (hinted in #19) is not wired here - review mode still uses the auto-approve reviewer until interactive stdin review is built.

changes.title: feat(output): store all audience texts in changelog.json
changes.description:
Closes #22

## What

Keeps the customer and product-manager texts in `changelog.json`, backed up inside the one file rather than scattered as marketing files in the repo.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `ChangelogDocument` gains a `renderings` object keyed by audience (`technical` / `customer` / `product`), written in a fixed order. `ChangelogJsonSerializer.Serialize` and the `IChangelogJsonWriter` port take an optional renderings map. When none are provided, the object is present but empty.
- The change entries stay deterministic facts; only the `renderings` are LLM-produced text.
- `docs/changelog-json.md` documents the new field.

## Format

`schemaVersion` stays **1** - per the documented stability contract, adding an optional field is non-breaking. Old consumers ignore `renderings`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Customer and PM texts are stored in `changelog.json`.
- [x] No separate visible marketing files are written into the repo.
- [x] Tests: assert customer and PM texts are stored in changelog.json and no marketing files are written.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 144, Infrastructure 26): customer/product texts stored and round-tripped, `renderings` is an empty object when none are given, and the writer produces **only** `changelog.json` (asserted the output directory contains exactly that one file).

changes.title: feat(releases): write the generated text back to GitHub release notes
changes.description:
Closes #21

## What

Places the generated text where the release actually lives - the GitHub release notes.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `IReleaseNotesWriter` port (reuses `RepositoryCoordinates`).
- **`Chartula.Infrastructure`**: `GitHubReleaseNotesWriter` over the GitHub REST API (plain `HttpClient`, source-generated JSON - AOT-friendly):
  - `GET /releases/tags/{tag}` -> found: `PATCH /releases/{id}` (update in place); 404: `POST /releases` (create with `tag_name` + `body`).
  - Returns the release's `html_url`. API/network failures become clear `InvalidOperationException`s.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: registers the writer. The GitHub `HttpClient` setup is extracted into a shared **`GitHubHttpClientFactory`** used by both the PR reader (#4) and the release-notes writer.

## Update, not duplicate

GitHub keys a release by its tag, so re-running for the same tag hits the **found** path and updates that one release's notes - never a second release.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The generated text is written to the release's notes.
- [x] Re-running updates rather than duplicating.
- [x] Tests: cover writing and the update-not-duplicate path against a mocked release API.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 141, Infrastructure 24): create when no release exists (POST with `tag_name` + body), update the found release (`PATCH /releases/{id}`) without creating a second one, and the API-error / network-failure / blank-tag paths - all against a routing stub handler.

changes.title: feat(output): write CHANGELOG.md, prepend and preserve history
changes.description:
Closes #20

## What

Writes each release as a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md`, preserving history and never overwriting it.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `ChangelogMarkdownComposer` (pure logic) composes the new content from the existing file and a release:
  - the new section is **prepended** at the top;
  - existing sections are kept **verbatim**;
  - re-running the same tag **replaces that section in place** rather than duplicating it - idempotent, and it never reorders history.
  - a brand-new file gets a `# Changelog` title.
- **`IChangelogMarkdownWriter`** port in Core; **`FileChangelogMarkdownWriter`** in `Chartula.Infrastructure` reads the existing file and writes the composed result.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: registers the writer alongside the JSON writer.

Same split as `changelog.json` (#12): format logic in Core, file I/O in Infrastructure.

## Idempotency detail

Re-running a release replaces its section **in place** (keeping its position), so re-running an older release after a newer one doesn't move it above the newer one. Running the same release twice yields a byte-identical file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The new section is added at the top.
- [x] Existing content is preserved intact.
- [x] Running twice for the same release does not duplicate or corrupt the file.
- [x] Tests: cover prepend, history preservation, and idempotency when run twice for the same release.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 141, Infrastructure 19): new-file creation, prepend above existing history, verbatim preservation of earlier sections, idempotency on re-run, in-place replace without reordering, CRLF handling, blank-tag rejection; the file writer writes across runs with no duplication for the same release.

changes.title: feat(review): opt-in review mode for human sign-off of flagged passages
changes.description:
Closes #19

## What

Lets a maintainer review generated texts before publishing, rather than trusting blindly.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `IReviewCoordinator`/`ReviewCoordinator` gate each rendering on an opt-in toggle.
  - Review **off** (default): the text passes straight through, approved as-is; the reviewer is never consulted.
  - Review **on**: the item goes to an `IReviewer` who **approves** it as-is or returns an **edited** version. The coordinator returns that `ReviewDecision`; its `Text` is what gets written.
  - `ReviewPresentation` formats an item for a maintainer - the generated text followed by the flagged passages (findings from the rule-based #17 and thorough #18 checks) highlighted.
  - `AutoApproveReviewer` is the non-interactive default; the interactive console reviewer ships with the CLI command surface (#23).
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: binds the `Chartula:Review` toggle and registers the coordinator.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] An optional review mode presents generated texts with flagged passages highlighted (`ReviewPresentation`).
- [x] The reviewer can approve or edit before output is written (`ReviewDecision.Approve` / `.Edit`; the coordinator returns the resulting text).
- [x] Review mode is opt-in, not forced on every release (`ReviewOptions.Enabled` off by default; the coordinator skips the reviewer when off).
- [x] Tests: cover the approve and edit paths and that review mode is opt-in.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 134, Infrastructure 16): approve keeps the original, edit returns the corrected text, an off toggle skips the reviewer entirely, the option is off by default, and flagged passages are presented/highlighted. Config binding verified end-to-end via `Chartula__Review__Enabled=true`.

changes.title: feat(faithfulness): thorough second-pass LLM check with a toggle
changes.description:
Closes #18

## What

Catches subtle, meaning-level hallucinations that the rule-based check (#17) can't see - e.g. "bug fixed" rendered as "security hole closed".

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `IThoroughFaithfulnessChecker`/`ThoroughFaithfulnessChecker` runs a second LLM pass via `CheckFaithfulnessAsync`, turning the fact base into grounded facts and flagging unsupported claims. When the toggle is off - or there's nothing to check - it returns a faithful report with **no LLM call**.
- **Toggle:** `ThoroughFaithfulnessOptions(Enabled = true)` - on by default, disabled via the `Chartula:Faithfulness:Thorough` config key.
- **Prompt:** consistent with the partial-class pattern, the faithfulness prompt moves from an inline placeholder in `ChatModel` into `IChangelogPromptBuilder.BuildFaithfulnessPrompt`, with its text in the Prompts partial and an explicit meaning-level-distortion instruction.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: binds the toggle and registers the checker.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A second LLM pass checks the text semantically against the fact base.
- [x] Unsupported claims are flagged.
- [x] On by default; a single toggle can disable it.
- [x] Tests: cover flagging of unsupported claims via a stubbed second pass and the enable/disable toggle.

## Out of scope

Per the issue: removing the toggle or adding more granular check settings is deferred until there's observability data.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 128, Infrastructure 16): the second pass flags unsupported claims (stubbed model), feeds output + grounded facts, defaults on, and makes no call when disabled or when the output is empty; a prompt test covers the meaning-level instruction and the facts/output content. Toggle verified end-to-end via `Chartula__Faithfulness__Thorough=false`.

changes.title: feat(faithfulness): rule-based check that catches obvious hallucinations
changes.description:
Closes #17

## What

Catches crude hallucinations for free, before any LLM check, so obvious errors never ship.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `IRuleBasedFaithfulnessChecker`/`RuleBasedFaithfulnessChecker` checks the generated output against the fact base and returns a `FaithfulnessReport`. It flags:
  - a **number** in the output not present in the facts (allowed numbers include PR numbers, linked issues, and any number in titles/descriptions/tag);
  - a **quoted or backticked name** that doesn't appear in the facts (the usual shape of an invented API/feature/option name);
  - a **breaking-change claim** when no fact is marked breaking.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: registers the checker.

Flags are advisory - they surface passages for review (feeds review mode, #19), not hard failures. Uses source-generated regexes (AOT-friendly).

## Zero token cost, always on

The checker has **no `IChangelogModel` dependency** - it's constructed with no arguments, so there is structurally nothing to call and it costs zero tokens. It always runs (no toggle).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Numbers, feature names, or breaking-change claims not present in the fact base are flagged.
- [x] The check uses no LLM call (zero token cost).
- [x] It runs always, by default.
- [x] Tests: cover flagging of numbers, feature names, and breaking claims absent from the fact base, and confirm no LLM call is made.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 122, Infrastructure 16): flags an invented number / quoted name / breaking claim; passes fully-supported output; does not flag supported numbers, names, or a genuine breaking change; deterministic with no model dependency; empty output passes.

changes.title: feat(formatting): consistent formatting and tone per audience
changes.description:
Closes #16

## What

Makes each rendering read as one coherent document, regardless of how the individual PRs were written.

- **Formatting (deterministic, guaranteed):** `IChangelogFormatter`/`ChangelogFormatter` in `Chartula.Core` normalizes the model output with conservative, structure-preserving rules - normalized line endings, a single `- ` bullet marker, trimmed trailing whitespace, collapsed blank-line runs - while leaving non-bullet lines (headings, prose) intact. The generator applies it to **every** rendering, so formatting is consistent no matter what the model returns.
- **Tone (prompt):** a new prompt rule tells the model to write in one consistent voice and format and not to carry over an individual author's tone or phrasing.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: registers the formatter.

## Why split this way

Tone normalization can only come from the prompt (it's a language judgment). Formatting consistency is enforced deterministically in code - which is also what makes it **testable with a stubbed model**: feed messy output, assert normalized output.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Varied PR-author styles are normalized per audience (prompt: one consistent voice, no author tone carried over).
- [x] Formatting is consistent within each rendering (deterministic formatter on every rendering).
- [x] Tests: assert formatting is consistent within each rendering.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 114, Infrastructure 16): bullet/spacing/whitespace/blank-line normalization, headings left intact, idempotency, the generator applying the formatter to model output, and the consistent-voice instruction present in the prompt.

changes.title: feat(rendering): render technical, customer, and PM from one fact base
changes.description:
Closes #15

## What

Produces the technical, customer, and product-manager versions of a release from **one** fact base, so they can never contradict each other.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `IReleaseRenderer`/`ReleaseRenderer` renders all three audiences from the same `FactBase`, delegating to the generator (one call per audience) and returning a result per `Audience`. A failure in one audience does not fail the others.
- **Generator**: audience selection is deterministic (in code, not the LLM):
  - **Customer** omits non-user-visible changes and their links.
  - **Technical** keeps the pull request link and the full change set.
  - **Product** sees the full set.
- **Prompt** (from #14): technical guidance now also asks to keep links; customer is benefit-focused, PM groups by theme.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: registers the renderer.

## Why they can't contradict

Every audience is derived from the same `FactBase` - the same established, deterministic facts. Each audience view is a selection over that one source, so there is no way for two renderings to disagree on what changed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] All three renderings come from the same fact base.
- [x] Technical keeps jargon, links, and precise breaking changes.
- [x] Customer is benefit-focused and omits non-user-visible changes.
- [x] PM is grouped by theme.
- [x] Tests: assert all three renderings derive from the same fact base and honor their audience rules (with a stubbed model).

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 105, Infrastructure 16): all three derive from the same base, technical keeps links + the full set, customer drops the internal change and carries no links, PM sees the full set, and one failed audience leaves the others intact - all via a stubbed model, no live call.

changes.title: refactor(prompting): move prompt text into a partial class
changes.description:
## What

Separates the prompt **text** from the prompt **build logic**, so all prompt strings live in one place and iterating on the wording is text-only work.

`ChangelogPromptBuilder` is now a `partial` class split across two files:
- **`ChangelogPromptBuilder.Prompts.cs`** - the prompt strings only (system header, the four rules, per-audience guidance).
- **`ChangelogPromptBuilder.cs`** - the composition logic, referencing those constants.

## Why

When iterating on prompts (which happens often), you now open one file with just the text - no navigating through composition logic to find and change a string.

## Pure refactor

The prompt text is **byte-for-byte unchanged**. The prompt-content assertions from #14 pass without any modification, which is the proof there is no behaviour change.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green and unchanged (Core 100, Infrastructure 16).

changes.title: feat(prompting): prompt architecture that rephrases facts, never invents
changes.description:
Closes #14

## What

Turns the placeholder prompt from #2 into a first-class, testable prompt architecture that keeps the output trustworthy.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `IChangelogPromptBuilder`/`ChangelogPromptBuilder` producing a `ChangelogPrompt` (system + user).
  - **System prompt** pins the model to rephrasing: never introduce a fact/number/name not in the list; treat each fact's category and `(breaking)` marker as **established** (use as given, don't change or infer); on thin facts stay brief and do not pad, speculate, or invent; no preamble/conclusion. Plus per-audience guidance.
  - **User prompt** carries only the facts - nothing our code adds to pad them.
  - `ChatModel` now delegates to the builder and just wires the prompt into the `IChatClient`.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: registers the builder in the LLM composition.

Categories and flags reach the model as text embedded by the generator (#13); the prompt presents them verbatim and instructs the model not to decide them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Prompts feed the fact base in and get rephrasing out.
- [x] Categories and flags are provided to the model, not decided by it.
- [x] Given thin facts, the output stays sparse rather than inventing detail (instructed in the system prompt; our code does not pad thin facts).
- [x] Tests: assert prompts feed the fact base and flags in, and that thin facts keep the output sparse (using a fake/recorded model).

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 100, Infrastructure 16): facts + flags reach the prompt, the rephrase-only / category-established / stay-sparse instructions are present, a thin fact base is not padded (`- Fix: a bug` verbatim), empty facts give an empty user prompt, and the prompt is tailored per audience. `ChatModel` tests updated for the new constructor (includes a null-prompt-builder guard).

changes.title: feat(generation): generate a changelog through the provider interface
changes.description:
Closes #13

## What

Makes generation actually work through the provider seam from #2, while staying provider-agnostic.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `IReleaseChangelogGenerator`/`ReleaseChangelogGenerator` and `ChangelogGenerationResult`.
  - Turns the fact base into grounded fact statements and makes **exactly one** `IChangelogModel.RephraseAsync` call per release.
  - An empty fact base makes **no call at all**.
  - Provider failures are caught and returned as a failed result (carrying the release tag and the provider message); cancellation propagates rather than being swallowed.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: registers the generator over the existing LLM services.

The generator depends only on `IChangelogModel` - no provider type is referenced. Prompt design (#14) and audience-specific rendering (#15) are out of scope here; the fact-to-statement mapping is a plain fact carrier.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A real call is made through the provider interface (`IChangelogModel.RephraseAsync`).
- [x] Errors are handled gracefully (provider failures -> failed `ChangelogGenerationResult`, not a crash).
- [x] Calls are minimal (exactly one per release; zero for an empty fact base).
- [x] Tests: cover the error-handling path using a fake provider (no live call).

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 89, Infrastructure 16): the single successful call, grounded-facts feeding, the provider-failure path, the empty-fact-base no-call, and cancellation propagation - all via a fake `IChangelogModel`, no live call.

changes.title: feat(serialization): write the fact base to changelog.json
changes.description:
Closes #12

## What

Writes the release fact base to `changelog.json` as a durable, machine-readable record and a source for later outputs (widget #32, RSS #33, audience texts #22).

- **`Chartula.Core`**:
  - `ChangelogDocument` - the stable on-disk shape (`schemaVersion` + `tag` + `changes`), kept **separate from the domain `FactBase`** so the domain can evolve without breaking the file format.
  - `ChangelogJsonSerializer` - `FactBase` -> JSON (and back). Pure, deterministic, source-generated (AOT/trim-safe); category written as its name for a stable, readable record.
  - `IChangelogJsonWriter` port.
- **`Chartula.Infrastructure`**: `FileChangelogJsonWriter` writes `changelog.json` to a directory (file I/O only; format lives in Core).
- **`docs/changelog-json.md`**: documents the schema, field types, and the stability contract.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: registers the writer.

## Format & stability

`schemaVersion` (currently `1`) is the contract - consumers read it and reject versions they don't understand. Fields are always present, including `null` values; adding optional fields is non-breaking, removing/renaming/re-meaning bumps the version. Every field is a deterministic fact - nothing in the file is LLM-generated.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The fact base is written to `changelog.json`.
- [x] The format is stable and documented (`docs/changelog-json.md`, versioned via `schemaVersion`).
- [x] The file is valid, parseable JSON.
- [x] Tests: assert the written changelog.json is valid, parseable, and matches the documented format.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 84, Infrastructure 16): serializer output is valid/parseable JSON matching the documented shape (top-level and per-change fields, category-as-name, `null` handling) and round-trips; the file writer writes to a temp dir, the file parses and round-trips, and missing directories are created.

changes.title: feat(facts): make fact-base depth configurable
changes.description:
Closes #11

## What

Lets a maintainer choose how much source material feeds the fact base, to fit their team's PR style.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `FactBaseDepth` with three modes plus `FactBaseDepthParser`.
  - `TitleOnly` - title only.
  - `TitleAndDescription` - **the default** (title + description, no issues).
  - `TitleDescriptionAndIssues` - title + description + linked issues.
  - `FactBaseBuilder` honours the depth: description from the middle mode up, linked issues only in the deepest mode.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: reads `Chartula:FactBase:Depth` and passes the parsed value into the builder. Parser accepts the canonical names plus aliases (`title`, `description`, `full`) and raises a clear error on an unknown value.

Because a depth is a config value (an enum), it is passed into the builder via a factory rather than registered as its own DI service.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Three modes: title-only / title + PR description / + linked issues.
- [x] Default is the middle mode (title + description, no issues).
- [x] The mode is set in configuration (`Chartula:FactBase:Depth`; sourced from `chartula.yaml` in #24).
- [x] Tests: cover all three depth modes and the default selection.

## Out of scope

Per the issue: whether all three modes survive long-term is revisited with real data; the option set is not expanded here.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 79, Infrastructure 12): the three depth behaviours and the parser (names, aliases, default, unknown-value error). Verified end-to-end: default and a `title-only` override both start cleanly, and an unknown depth fails at startup with a clear error.

changes.title: feat(facts): transform curated changes into the release fact base
changes.description:
Closes #10

## What

Assembles the complete, grounded fact base for a release, tying together everything built so far.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `IFactBaseBuilder`/`FactBaseBuilder` and the `FactBase` container (tag + one `ChangeFact` per included change).
  - Resolves changes with the missing-PR fallback (#5), drops filtered-out changes (#8), and maps each survivor to a `ChangeFact`.
  - Category and breaking flag come from deterministic categorization (#6); a label can force the category (#7).
  - `IsUserVisible` is derived from the category (outward-facing categories, plus every breaking change).
  - `LinkedIssues` are parsed from GitHub closing keywords (`closes/fixes/resolves #n`) in the title and body.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: registers the builder.

**Category and flags come from the deterministic curation steps, never from an LLM** - the builder has no LLM dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Each curated PR maps to one fact object.
- [x] Category and flags come from the curation step, not the LLM.
- [x] The result is a complete fact base for the release.
- [x] Tests: cover the curated-PR to fact-object mapping over representative inputs.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 64, Infrastructure 12): PR-to-fact mapping with curated category/flags and linked-issue extraction, exclusion of filtered changes, user-visible resolution (incl. the breaking-change override), a label-forced category rescuing a chore, and the commit-data fallback.

changes.title: feat(facts): define the fact-base data model (index card per change)
changes.description:
Closes #9

## What

Defines `ChangeFact` in **`Chartula.Core`** - one structured object per change, the single source of truth the LLM may only rephrase from.

Captures the established facts:
- title, PR number, link
- category (from deterministic categorization)
- user-visible flag, breaking flag
- linked issues
- an optional description (populated per the fact-base depth, #11)

Every field is derived deterministically; **nothing in the model is LLM-generated**. PR-only fields (number, link) are nullable so commit-based changes fit the same shape.

## Notes

- This is the per-change "index card". The release-level container is assembled when curated PRs are transformed into facts (#10), and the whole base is serialized to `changelog.json` in #12.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A data model captures: PR title, number, link, category, user-visible flag, breaking flag, linked issues.
- [x] The model is serializable.
- [x] Nothing in the model is LLM-generated - it holds established facts only.
- [x] Tests: cover serialization round-trip of the data model.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 58, Infrastructure 12): round-trip for a PR-based fact, a commit-based fact with no PR, and round-trip stability.

changes.title: feat(filtering): drop internal/chore changes by default
changes.description:
Closes #8

## What

Keeps the changelog relevant by filtering out internal/chore changes, combining the deterministic categorization (#6) and label rules (#7).

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `IChangeFilter`/`ChangeFilter` and `ChangeFilterRules`.
  - Decision order: a label that excludes the change wins outright -> a breaking change is never dropped -> otherwise the change is dropped when its **effective category** (a label-forced one, else the deterministic one) is in the excluded set.
  - Default excluded set: `Internal`. Overridable via config - an explicit (possibly empty) list replaces the default.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: binds the `Chartula:Filter` section and registers the filter.

## Decision

**A breaking change is never dropped**, even if its category is excluded - a deterministic safeguard from the breaking flag (not guesswork), matching the intent to show breaking changes prominently (#25). An explicit label exclusion still wins over it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Internal/chore changes are excluded by default.
- [x] Defaults are overridable in config (`Chartula:Filter:ExcludeCategories`).
- [x] Filtering is based on category and labels, not guesswork.
- [x] Tests: cover default exclusion of internal/chore changes and config overrides.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 55, Infrastructure 12): default internal/chore exclusion, user-facing categories kept, both config overrides, label exclusion, forced-category-into-excluded, only-labeled, the breaking safeguard, and label-exclusion precedence. Config validated end-to-end: an unknown `Chartula:Filter` category name fails at startup with a clear error.

changes.title: feat(labels): steer curation with label rules from config
changes.description:
Closes #7

## What

Lets a maintainer steer curation with GitHub labels, controlled from config, without touching code.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `LabelRules` (excluded labels, label -> category overrides, only-include-labeled mode) plus `ILabelRulePolicy`/`LabelRulePolicy`, which produce a `LabelDecision` (include + optional forced category).
  - Precedence: exclusion wins; then only-labeled drops unlabeled changes; otherwise included, with the first matching label deciding a forced category.
  - All optional: `LabelRules.None` ignores labels entirely, so the tool works with no labels at all. Matching is case-insensitive.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: binds the `Chartula:Labels` section into `LabelRules` via `LabelRules.From` (parses category names, clear error on an unknown one) and registers the policy.

The rules come from configuration now; **#24** wires `chartula.yaml` as a config source and the binding is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A label can exclude a PR from the changelog.
- [x] A label can force a PR into a given category.
- [x] An "only include labeled PRs" mode is possible.
- [x] All of this is optional - the tool works with no labels at all.
- [x] Rules are read from configuration (`Chartula:Labels`; sourced from `chartula.yaml` in #24).
- [x] Tests: cover exclusion, forced category mapping, only-labeled mode, and the no-labels default, driven from config.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 41, Infrastructure 12). Config binding verified end-to-end: a valid `Chartula:Labels` config starts cleanly, and an unknown category name (`Chartula__Labels__Category__security=bogus`) fails at startup with a clear error listing the valid categories.

changes.title: feat(categorization): assign categories deterministically before the LLM
changes.description:
Closes #6

## What

Decides the kind of each change in code, before any generation, so the model can never invent what kind of change something is.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `IChangeCategorizer` + `ConventionalCommitCategorizer`.
  - Reads Conventional Commit conventions from the change title (`type(scope)!: subject`).
  - `ChangeCategory`: Feature (`feat`), Fix (`fix`), Performance (`perf`), Documentation (`docs`), Refactor (`refactor`), Internal (`build`/`ci`/`chore`/`test`/`style`/`revert`), and **Other** as the sane default for unrecognized/prefix-less titles.
  - Breaking is tracked **separately** (`ChangeClassification.IsBreaking`) via a `!` marker, a `breaking` type, or a `BREAKING CHANGE` body note - so a breaking feature stays a feature but is still flagged (useful for the "show breaking prominently" config in #25).
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: registers the categorizer alongside the resolver.

Pure and deterministic - no LLM, no I/O. Uses a source-generated regex (AOT-friendly).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Conventional-commit prefixes (feat/fix/breaking, etc.) are detected.
- [x] Each change is assigned a category deterministically.
- [x] Unrecognized changes get a sane default category (`Other`).
- [x] No LLM call is involved in this step.
- [x] Tests: cover prefix detection, deterministic assignment, and the default for unrecognized changes.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 33, Infrastructure 12): per-type prefix detection, scopes, case-insensitivity, all three breaking markers, the `Other` default, and determinism.

changes.title: feat(curation): degrade gracefully when clean PRs are missing
changes.description:
Closes #5

## What

Makes the pipeline still produce something useful when PR discipline is imperfect.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: `IReleaseChangeResolver` + `ReleaseChangeResolver` turn a `CommitRange` and the merged `PullRequestInfo` list into `ReleaseChange` values (title, description, number, url, labels, `ChangeSource`, commit sha). Pure domain logic, no I/O.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: registers the resolver (dependency-free singleton).

## Behaviour

- Merged PRs present -> one change per PR (`Source = PullRequest`).
- No PRs at all -> one change per commit, using the commit subject (`Source = Commit`).
- Blank/uninformative PR title (e.g. `WIP`, `update`, `Merge ...`) -> falls back to the PR body's first informative line, then to a generic `PR #n`.
- Empty release -> empty set, never an exception.

The uninformative-title heuristic is a small starter set; it becomes configurable with the config work (#25).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] With no associated PRs, the tool falls back to commit data.
- [x] With empty/uninformative PR titles, it uses the best available source.
- [x] The tool never hard-fails solely because PR discipline is imperfect.
- [x] Tests: cover each fallback path (no PRs, empty/uninformative titles) and confirm no hard failure.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 13, Infrastructure 12): PR-preferred path, commit fallback, blank-title -> body, uninformative-title -> body (theory), number fallback, and the empty-release no-op.

changes.title: feat(pull-requests): fetch merged PRs for a release from the GitHub API
changes.description:
Closes #4

## What

Summarizes changes per merged PR instead of per raw commit.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: the `IReleasePullRequestReader` port plus `PullRequestInfo` (number, title, description, labels, url) and `RepositoryCoordinates`. Pure domain.
- **`Chartula.Infrastructure`**: `GitHubPullRequestReader` - for the commits in a `CommitRange`, queries GitHub's "pull requests associated with a commit" endpoint, keeps merged PRs only, de-duplicates by number. DTOs parsed via a source-generated `System.Text.Json` context.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: composition root configures the `HttpClient` (base URL, GitHub headers, bearer token by env-var name) and registers the reader.

## Decisions

- **Raw `HttpClient` + `System.Text.Json` source-gen over Octokit** - dependency-light and native-AOT friendly (#39), consistent with the git-CLI choice in #3. The stub `HttpMessageHandler` makes it fully mockable without network.
- Token read by env-var name (`GITHUB_TOKEN`), optional (public repos work unauthenticated, subject to rate limits).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] For the commit range, associated merged PRs are retrieved.
- [x] Each PR yields title, description, labels, number, and link.
- [x] API failures produce a clear error, not a crash (API status, network, and malformed-response paths all raise a clear `InvalidOperationException`).
- [x] Tests: cover PR retrieval and field extraction against mocked GitHub responses, including the API-failure path.

## Verification

Build 0 warnings / 0 errors. Tests green (Core 5, Infrastructure 12): field mapping, merged-only filtering, de-duplication across commits, empty-range no-op, and the API/network/malformed error paths.

Out of scope (own issue): fallback when clean PRs are missing (#5).

changes.title: feat(history): read the commit range for a release from git
changes.description:
Closes #3

## What

Finds exactly the commits belonging to a release.

- **`Chartula.Core`**: the `IReleaseCommitReader` port plus `CommitInfo` and `CommitRange` (with `IsFirstRelease`). Pure domain, no I/O.
- **`Chartula.Infrastructure`** (new layer): `GitCliCommitReader` shells out to `git` - the range since the previous tag (`<prev>..<tag>`), or all history up to the tag when there is no previous tag (first release). Clear errors for unknown/blank tags.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: composition root registers the git reader; the pipeline depends only on the port.

## Decisions

- **git CLI over LibGit2Sharp**: avoids native deps that would fight the planned native-AOT binaries (#39). `git` is present in any repo Chartula runs on.
- **New `Chartula.Infrastructure` layer** for concrete I/O adapters, keeping `Core` pure domain and `Cli` a thin composition root. Future home for the GitHub API (#4), file writers (#12/#20/#21), and webhooks (#28).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Given a tag, the commit range since the previous tag is determined.
- [x] Works when there is no previous tag (first release -> all history).
- [x] The commit set is available as input to the next stage (`CommitRange.Commits`, resolvable via `IReleaseCommitReader`).
- [x] Tests: cover the commit-range calculation, including the first-release case with no previous tag.

## Verification

Tests run the real `git` CLI against throwaway repositories (deterministic, offline): between-tags range, first-release fallback, sha/subject mapping, unknown-tag and blank-tag errors. Build 0 warnings / 0 errors; all tests green (Core 5, Infrastructure 6).

changes.title: feat(llm): abstract the LLM provider behind IChangelogModel
changes.description:
Closes #2

## What

Adds the provider-agnostic LLM seam the pipeline builds on.

- **`Chartula.Core`** (new): the domain-focused seam.
  - `IChangelogModel` - the interface the pipeline depends on (`RephraseAsync`, `CheckFaithfulnessAsync`).
  - `ChatModel` - the single implementation, backed by a provider-agnostic `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.IChatClient`.
  - Domain types: `Audience`, `GroundedFacts`, `RephraseRequest`, `FaithfulnessRequest`, `FaithfulnessReport`.
- **`Chartula.Cli`**: composition root wiring Anthropic as the first provider (`AsIChatClient`), model + provider selectable via config, API key read by env-var name. This is the only provider-specific code.
- **`Chartula.Core.Tests`** (new): 5 tests exercising the seam with a stub `IChatClient` - no live provider call.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] An interface defines the LLM operations the pipeline needs.
- [x] At least one concrete provider implements it.
- [x] The rest of the code depends only on the interface.
- [x] API keys are read from environment/config, never hardcoded.
- [x] Tests: the seam is exercised with a stub IChatClient (no live provider call), asserting the pipeline uses only the interface.

## Notes

- Architecture chosen after discussion: hybrid (domain interface over agnostic `IChatClient`). Swapping providers is a composition-root change only.
- `GroundedFacts` and the `ChatModel` prompts are intentionally minimal placeholders; the fact base and prompt design are their own issues.

Build: 0 warnings / 0 errors. `dotnet test`: 5/5 green.

renderings.customer:
### What needs action
- **Breaking: Configuring categories**: For readers using custom category names, the category configuration section requires explicit ordering and display names to be set in `chartula.yaml`, so unknown category names will no longer be accepted by the parser.

### What's New
- **Run metrics summary**: For anyone running preview and generate, you can now see rule-based check runs, thorough check findings, and token usage counts at the end of each run, so you no longer have to guess the cost of your checks.
- **Category settings**: For readers customizing their changelog, you can now configure category order, display names, and breaking-change prominence in `chartula.yaml`, so you no longer have to rely on default presentation rules.
- **YAML configuration**: For readers running the tool without environment variables, `chartula.yaml` or `.yml` files are now loaded and flattened into configuration keys before environment overrides, so you can now rely on storing your preferences in a file.
- **CLI commands**: For command-line users, `chartula preview` and `chartula generate` commands are now wired to run the release pipeline with `--tag` and `--repo` options, so you no longer have to run the pipeline without a user interface.
- **Release notes publishing**: For maintainers publishing updates, generated text is now written directly to GitHub release notes via `IReleaseNotesWriter`, so you no longer have to copy and paste text manually into GitHub releases.
- **Changelog history preservation**: For anyone maintaining a changelog file, new releases are now prepended to `CHANGELOG.md` while preserving earlier history intact, so you no longer have to worry about overwriting previous release entries.
- **Review mode**: For maintainers wanting manual quality checks, an opt-in review mode now presents generated texts with flagged passages highlighted so you can approve or edit them before output is written, so you no longer have to publish generated text without review.
- **Thorough faithfulness check**: For readers verifying semantic accuracy, a second-pass LLM check now runs by default to flag unsupported claims and meaning-level distortions against the fact base, so you no longer have to manually cross-check every sentence.
- **Rule-based faithfulness check**: For readers wanting instant error detection, a rule-based checker now runs by default to catch numbers, quoted names, and breaking claims absent from the fact base without any LLM cost, so you no longer have to ship obvious hallucinations.
- **Multi-audience rendering**: For teams publishing different views, technical, customer, and product-manager versions of a release can now be rendered from a single fact base, so you no longer have to write separate release descriptions by hand.
- **Prompt architecture**: For readers relying on accurate rephrasing, prompts now enforce strict rephrasing rules that prevent the model from inventing facts, so you no longer have to inspect outputs for hallucinated details.
- **Fact generation**: For anyone generating release changelogs, generators now translate grounded facts into a single rephrasing call per release, so you no longer have to make redundant model requests.
- **Configurable fact-base depth**: For teams with different PR styles, the fact-base depth can now be configured to choose between title-only, title and description, or full inclusion including linked issues, so you no longer have to accept a fixed level of detail.
- **Fact-base transformation**: For anyone compiling a release, curated changes are now transformed into a complete, deterministic fact base where categories and flags come from curation rules rather than guesses, so you no longer have to manually structure raw commits.
- **Change fact data model**: For developers inspecting structured release data, `ChangeFact` now captures titles, PR numbers, links, categories, user-visible flags, breaking flags, and linked issues in a serializable index card, so you no longer have to parse raw strings.
- **Change filtering**: For readers viewing clean changelogs, internal and chore changes are now dropped by default using effective categories and label rules, so you no longer have to wade through internal commits.
- **Label rules**: For teams using GitHub labels, curation can now be steered via configuration rules that exclude PRs, force categories, or restrict output to labeled items, so you no longer have to manually filter commits.
- **Deterministic categorization**: For anyone categorizing updates, conventional commit prefixes are now detected deterministically into categories like feature, fix, or breaking without an LLM, so you no longer have to guess the intent of a commit.
- **PR resolution fallback**: For repositories with imperfect pull request discipline, resolvers now fall back to commit data or uninformative-title heuristics when clean PRs are missing, so you no longer have to fail builds over missing pull requests.
- **GitHub PR reading**: For maintainers linking code changes to pull requests, associated merged PRs are now retrieved from the GitHub API using raw `HttpClient` and source-generated JSON, so you no longer have to rely on heavy client libraries.
- **Commit range reading**: For users tracking release history, commit ranges between tags or all history for a first release are now read directly via the git CLI, so you no longer have to manually specify commit hashes.
- **LLM provider abstraction**: For developers configuring model backends, the LLM operations are now abstracted behind an `IChangelogModel` interface with Anthropic wired as the default provider, so you no longer have to couple your code to a single vendor.

### Bug Fixes
- **Truncation in LLM responses**: For anyone running text generation, requests now send a configured maximum output ceiling (`llm.maxOutputTokens`) instead of falling back to default limits, so you no longer have to deal with audience texts cut off mid-word.
- **False breaking changes in categorizer**: For teams writing release notes, breaking changes are now detected strictly via conventional commit footers (`BREAKING CHANGE`) rather than case-insensitive body substrings, so you no longer have to correct mislabelled features caused by normal prose discussions.

### Also:
- Also: `Chartula.Core/Observability/` provides `IRunMetrics`, `NullRunMetrics`, `RunReport`, and `RunReportFormatter`.
- Also: `ChatModel` attributes token usage per `LlmOperation` and counts providers reporting no usage.
- Also: `ReleasePipeline` records both checks' findings in one call and returns the report on `ReleaseOutcome`.
- Also: Measurement operates as an optional side channel where runs without a sink produce byte-identical output.
- Also: `docs/run-metrics.md` explains how to read the summary and make the keep-or-drop call.

renderings.product:
### [Observability]
- Every `preview` and `generate` run now concludes with a metric summary detailing run counts, findings, claims, and token counts, so decisions can be driven by data instead of guesswork.
- Token usage is now tracked per operation and reported alongside optional invocation metrics, so performance and cost remain visible without altering outputs.

### [Configuration]
- Category presentation and filtering are now configurable through standalone sections alongside existing settings, so the layout matches repository needs without code changes.
- Configuration files are now loaded with sensible defaults and environment variable overrides, so the tool runs out of the box while staying adaptable.

### [Pipeline]
- The technical, customer, and product-manager renderings are now produced from a single shared fact base, so different audiences never receive contradictory change descriptions.
- The command-line interface now wires execution commands directly to the core release pipeline, so technical and summary output can be previewed or written reliably.

### [Serialization]
- Audience-specific text renderings are now stored directly inside the changelog document, so marketing files are centralized without scattering individual artifacts across the repository.
- Generated changelog entries are now prepended to existing history in place, so previous release records are preserved without duplication or reordering.

### [Releases]
- Release notes are now written directly to GitHub tags and updated in place upon re-runs, so target release pages always reflect current change documentation.

### [Review]
- Generated passages can now be interactively reviewed and edited before publishing, so maintainers retain final approval authority over model-generated text.

### [Faithfulness]
- A semantic second-pass checker now evaluates generated output against grounded facts using an optional toggle, so subtle meaning-level hallucinations are caught.
- A rule-based checker now evaluates numbers, names, and breaking-change claims against facts with zero token cost, so obvious errors are caught before any language model invocation.

### [Formatting]
- Model outputs are now normalized using structure-preserving rules alongside prompt instructions, so every rendering reads with a consistent voice regardless of author style.

### [Prompting]
- Prompts now constrain models strictly to rephrasing established facts without padding thin details, so generated text remains trustworthy and sparse.

### [Generation]
- Release facts are now mapped to structured statements and transformed via abstract model interfaces, so generation handles provider failures gracefully.

### [Fact Base]
- Fact bases are now serialized into stable, versioned JSON schemas, so downstream consumers maintain a reliable machine-readable record.
- Fact base depth is now configurable across three modes, so maintainers can tailor source material volume to match their team styles.
- Curated pull requests are now transformed into structured fact objects carrying deterministic categories and user-visible flags, so outputs rely on code rather than inference.
- Change data models now capture structured index cards per change, so downstream consumers access clean single sources of truth.

### [Filtering]
- Internal and chore changes are now excluded by default through deterministic label and category rules, so release notes remain focused on customer-visible updates.

### [Labels]
- Curation can now be steered through configuration rules that exclude changes or force categories by label, so teams can guide outputs without modifying code.

### [Categorization]
- Change types and breaking flags are now assigned deterministically from conventional commit prefixes prior to model generation, so kinds of change are never invented.

### [Pull Requests]
- Commit ranges are now resolved to merged pull requests with fallback heuristics for missing titles, so the pipeline produces useful summaries despite imperfect PR discipline.
- Associated merged pull requests are now fetched for release commit ranges from the GitHub API, so summaries represent PRs instead of raw commits.

### [History]
- Release commit ranges are now read directly from git repositories via command-line invocations, so exact sets of release changes are identified offline.

### [LLM]
- Language model operations are now abstracted behind an agnostic provider interface, so backing models can be swapped via composition roots.
